Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

The Tafsir of Surah al-Hijr, and it is Meccan.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Alif. Lam. Ra.﴾ Its meaning: "I am Allah, the All-Seeing" (Ana Allahu Ara). It was also said: "Alif. Lam. Ra", "Ha. Mim", and "Nun" are [in meaning] "the Most Merciful" (al-Rahman).

﴿These are the verses of the Book﴾ Its meaning: these are the verses of the Book.

﴿And a clear Qur'an﴾ Its meaning: that it makes clear the lawful from the unlawful, and the truth from the falsehood. If someone says: "The Qur'an is the Book, and the Book is the Qur'an, so what is the benefit of combining the two?"

The answer: each of them conveys a meaning that the other does not convey. The Book (al-Kitab) is that which is written, and the Qur'an (al-Qur'an) is that which gathers some of it together with other parts. It was also said: the intended meaning of "the Book" is the Torah and the Gospel, and "the Qur'an" is that which Allah, Exalted is He, sent down upon Muhammad (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 2:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Perhaps those who disbelieved will wish they had been Muslims.﴾ Know that kam (كم) is used for multiplication, and rubba (رب) for diminution. It is also said that rubbama (رُبمَا) is used with emphasis (tashdid), rubama with lightening (takhfif), and rubtama (ربتما) with the taa' (ت), all with one meaning. The poet said:

(Mawiyy, O rubtama a raid... sweeping like a branding of the iron)

Some have distinguished between rubba and rubama, saying: rubba enters upon the noun and rubama upon the verb. So one says: rubba man (رب رجل) came to me, and one says: rubama came to me (رُبمَا جَاءَنِي).

Scholars differed concerning the situation in which the disbelievers will wish this, and wadd (الود) is tamanni (wishing).

The first view: it is at the time of witnessing (al-mu'aynah), and this is the view of al-Dahhak.

The second view: it is on the Day of Resurrection.

The third view, which is the most well-known: it is when God brings the believers out of the Fire. In the transmitted reports narrated by Abu Musa al-Ash'ari from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "God will cause a people from the people of the qiblah to enter the Fire along with the disbelievers, and they will remain in it as long as God wills. The disbelievers will say to them: 'Are you Muslims?' They will say: 'Yes.' The disbelievers will say: 'Your Islam has not benefited you at all, and you are with us in the Fire.' They will say: 'We committed sins and were seized for them.' God, exalted is He, hears all of that, and He says: 'Bring out of the Fire whoever was a Muslim' — and in another narration: 'whoever said: there is no god but God' — and they will come out. Then the disbelievers will wish they had been Muslims." And in some narrations: "When the disbelievers say this statement to the Muslims, God, exalted is He, becomes angry at their saying, so He says: 'Bring out...,' as we have explained."

If someone says: If rubama is for diminution, how can their wishing be little, when we know in reality that all of them wish this, and that this wishing from them is frequent?

The answer: The Arabs may mention this expression while intending multiplication. A speaker says to another: "Perhaps you will regret this action," while he knows that regret over it is frequent from him, and the meaning is: if you regretted a little, the little regret would suffice to make you refrain from it, so how much more so the great? 

The second answer: their preoccupation with the punishment does not leave them free for regret, and at some moments this regret may occur to them and cross their minds.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 3:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves, and let hope distract them﴾, and so on. This is a threat and a warning. "Eating" is well known. As for "tamattu'" (enjoyment), it is taking pleasure in seeking it moment after moment, (like "al-ta'arrub"), which is seeking it moment after moment. His saying: ﴿and let hope distract them﴾ means: hope occupies them away from the Hereafter.

His saying: ﴿But they will come to know﴾ is another threat. Some scholars have said: "Leave them" is a threat, and His saying ﴿But they will come to know﴾ is another threat. So when does life become pleasant between two threats?
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We did not destroy any town except that it had a known decree﴾. That is: a term appointed, which it can neither precede nor delay.

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿No community can precede its appointed term, nor can they delay it﴾. Its meaning is that the appointed punishment does not come before its time, nor is it delayed beyond its time. It has also been said: this refers to death, that it neither precedes nor is delayed beyond its appointed time.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 6:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they say: O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down, indeed you are mad.﴾ "The Reminder" is the Qur'an. And His saying, ﴿indeed you are mad﴾, is their address to the Prophet.

And His saying, "﴿O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down﴾," they only said it in a manner of mockery, because if they had said it in a manner of certainty, they would have believed in it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 7:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Why do you not bring us the angels?﴾ Meaning: "Why not (halla) bring us the angels?"

The poet said:

(You count the (qa'r) of the she-camels as the best of your glory... O sons of (Tutabri), were it not for the armored, mail-clad warrior!)

Meaning: "Why do you not count the mail-clad warrior?"

And his statement: ﴿If you are of the truthful﴾ means: that you are a Prophet.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 8:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿We do not send down the angels except with truth﴾. The truth with which the angels descend is revelation, the taking of the souls of the servants, the destruction of the disbelievers, the recording of deeds, and what is similar to that.

And His words: ﴿Nor would they have been given respite﴾, meaning: delayed. The disbelievers used to ask for the angels to be sent down before their eyes, so Allah the Exalted answered them with this. Its meaning is: if they were to descend before their eyes, the respite would be removed from the disbelievers and they would be punished immediately.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 9:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions. The first: that We protect Muhammad (ﷺ). The second: that We protect the Qur'an, and this is the more fitting with the apparent wording. The meaning of the Qur'an's being protected is that it is preserved from addition to it or subtraction from it. God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it﴾, and "falsehood" here is Iblis. Its meaning is that Iblis cannot add to it what is not part of it, nor subtract from it what is part of it.

Almighty Allah's words: ﴿And We certainly sent (messengers) before you among the sects of the former peoples.﴾ Ash-shi'ah (sect, party): they are the people who gather together and whose word is unified. Its meaning here: among the nations of the former peoples.

"And His saying: ﴿And there comes not to them a messenger but that they used to mock him﴾. This is a consolation to the Prophet, and its meaning is: just as they mocked you, so too were the prophets before you mocked."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 12:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Thus do We cause it to enter into the hearts of the criminals.﴾ Al-Hasan said: "Thus do We cause shirk (associating partners with Allah) to enter into the hearts of the criminals." And "ntaslukuhu" means: We make it enter. Mujahid said: "We cause denial (al-takdhib) to enter." The kaf in ﴿kadhalika﴾ is the kaf of comparison (kaf al-tashbih), meaning: just as We did with the disbelievers before these, so do We do with these disbelievers.

Some of them have said: the meaning of His saying ﴿Thus do We cause it to enter﴾ is: We cause the Qur'an to enter, and its meaning is that when He gave them that by which they could understand the Qur'an, it was as if He had caused the Qur'an to enter into their hearts. The transmitted position from the early generations (al-salaf) is the first view, and it is an explicit refutation of the Qadariyya.

It is the saying of Allah: ﴿They do not believe in it﴾, meaning: in the Prophet and the Qur'an. ﴿And the way of the former peoples has already passed﴾, meaning: the way of the former peoples has passed on, and the way of the former peoples is the destruction that comes upon them when they deny the prophets.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And even if We opened for them a gate from the sky﴾. The meaning is apparent. And His saying: ﴿so that they continued to ascend through it﴾. It is said: "ẓalla (to continue) doing such-and-such" when one does it during the day, and "bāta (to spend the night) doing such-and-such" when one does it at night.

And His saying: ﴿ya'rujūn﴾ means "they ascend." It is said: "'araja ya'ruju" when one ascends, and "'araja ya'ruju" also when one becomes lame (a'raj). Opinions differ regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿fa-ẓallū﴾: the majority hold that they are the angels, and another view holds that they are the polytheists.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 15:

And His saying: ﴿They would surely say, "Our eyes have only been intoxicated (sukkirat)."﴾ It has been recited in two ways: "sukkirat" (with the first letter doubled, sukkirat) and "sukirat" (lightened). The meaning of the lightened form is: "sihirat" (were bewitched), and the meaning of the doubled form is: "sudda" (were blocked) and "ukhidhat" (were seized). It was also said: "amiyat" (were blinded). 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: it is derived from sukr (intoxication), meaning: just as intoxication clouds our minds, so this has clouded our eyes. And His saying: ﴿Nay, but we are a people who have been bewitched.﴾ That is: deceived (makhdu'un). It was also said its meaning is: sorcery has worked upon us.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 16:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And We have placed in the sky constellations (buruj)﴾. Al-Buruj: they are the great stars, and the word is derived from appearing (al-zuhur). It is said: "tabarrajat al-mar'ah" (the woman displayed herself) when she appeared. It is also said: they are the stations (al-manazil). It is also said: they are the twelve constellations (al-buruj al-ithna 'ashar). It is also said: they are the seven wandering stars (al-sab' al-sayyarah). And from 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi: they are palaces in the sky over which there are guards. His words: ﴿And We have adorned it for the observers﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 17:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We guarded it from every accursed devil﴾. Al-Kalbi mentioned that the heavens were not guarded from the devils before ʿĪsā (ʿAlayhi al-Salam). When ʿĪsā (ʿAlayhi al-Salam) was sent, three of the heavens were guarded, and when Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent, all the heavens were guarded. His saying, ﴿rajīm﴾, means: stoned (marjum). It was also said: accursed (malʿun). It was also said: reviler (shatīm).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 15, verse 18:

And the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Except one who steals a hearing﴾. Concerning this, the reports say that the devils mount one upon another up to the lowest heaven, and they steal hearing from the angels; so the stars pelt them, killing some and maiming others.

Scholars have differed over when they steal the hearing. One of the two opinions is that they steal the hearing from the angels in the heaven, and the other opinion is that they steal the hearing from the angels in the air. As for how the angels of the heaven come to know the matter, it is by their asking the angels of the second heaven; in this way the people of each heaven ask the people of the heaven above them, until they reach the bearers of the Throne, and they inform them of what Allah the Exalted has decreed. The news then returns from heaven to heaven until it reaches the lowest heaven, and then the devils steal it, as we have said before.

And His words: ﴿Then there pursues him a clear flaming fire﴾. The shihab (flaming fire) is a flame of fire. If someone says: "We do not see fire; we only see a light or a star that shoots down."

The answer: it is possible that it shoots down as a light, and when it reaches him it becomes fire; or it is possible that from a distance it appears to be a star while it is fire. It has also been said: the star shoots down, strikes the devil, and then returns to its place. Know that this did not appear openly in the times of the prophets before the Messenger, and no poet of the Arabs mentioned it before the time of the Prophet. Rather, it was narrated at the beginning of the Prophet's affair, and it was a foundation for his prophethood. Poets mentioned it only in his time. The poet said:

(As if it were a star following a demon ... marked out in the blackness of the night, shooting down.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 19:

The Most High's statement: ﴿And the earth — We have spread it out﴾ means: We have spread it out (basaṭnāhā). It is said: it extends five hundred years' journey in every direction, and it was spread out (duḥiyat) from beneath the Ka'bah.

And His statement: ﴿And We have cast into it firm mountains﴾ means: mountains that are fixed (thawābit). The earth used to tilt until God anchored it with the mountains.

And His statement: ﴿And We have caused to grow therein every thing in due measure﴾ means: known (ma'lūm). It is also said: "every thing in due measure" means: [such as] iron, lead, copper, gold, silver, and everything that is weighed.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 20:

As for His saying: ﴿And We have made for you therein means of livelihood﴾, it has been said: they are food, drink and clothing. It has also been said: they are whatever a person lives on in this world. Jarir said in verse:

(The livelihood of the family of Zayd keeps demanding of me... and where shall I find the maraqq and the sinab?)

The sinab are the fish-like ones (ḍibāb) from the ājar (the reed-like plants used for seasoning), and other such condiments (lawāmikh, relishes).

As for ﴿and [for] those for whom you are not providers﴾, its meaning is: We made therein means of livelihood for you, and We made therein [means of livelihood] for those whom you do not provide for, namely the beasts, the birds and the wild animals. There is another view regarding the verse: that We made for you therein means of livelihood, and We also made for you the beasts, the birds and the cattle, and We have taken care of their provision for you. If someone says: He has said, "those for whom you are not providers," and "man" (min) is used only for those who have reason, not for those who do not, [the answer is as follows].

The answer to this: the slaves and the owned persons have entered among these, and the Arabs, when they combine those who have reason with those who do not, give precedence to those who have reason.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 21:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasuries﴾. He means: its keys (mafatih) to its treasuries. It was also said: they are the treasuries themselves. The meaning of "treasuries" is that when He says "Be," it is.

His saying: ﴿And We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾. That is: except in a known measure at a known time. It is said: no drop of rain descends from the sky except that with it is an angel who drives it wherever Allah wills. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 22:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And We send the winds fertilizing﴾. Abu 'Ubayda said: mulaqih, its singular being mulaqqihah. Another said: they are lawaqih, its singular being laqih. The meaning of laqih is that they carry water, and the meaning of mulqih is that they pass over the clouds and the earth and thus fertilize them. The fertilizing of the clouds is that it casts into the clouds that by which they carry water. It was also said: they fertilize the trees as well.

Ibn Mas'ud said: the wind carries water and then makes the clouds flow, so the clouds yield their milk as a she-camel yields her milk. It is narrated from Ubayd ibn 'Umayr that he said: the bearing wind comes and sweeps the earth clean, then the wind that brings forth comes and brings forth the clouds, then the wind that gathers comes and gathers the clouds, one part to another, then the fertilizing wind comes and fertilizes the clouds. (And it is said in) that the fertilizing winds are the south wind.

In some reports: "No south wind blows except that it causes a spring to gush forth, abundant and plentiful." As for the barren wind (al-'aqim), it is the one that does not fertilize and brings punishment.

As for His words: ﴿And We send down water from the sky and give you to drink from it﴾, meaning: We gave you drink from it. It is said: asqa so-and-so when one provides him with a drink, and saqa so-and-so when one gives him what he may drink.

As for His words: ﴿And you are not its keepers﴾, meaning: it is in Our storehouses, not in yours. It was also said: and you are not those who can withhold it or prevent it (i.e., [even] if you desired it).

Almost all of this: the Almighty's saying, "Indeed it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the inheritors" (Q. 15:23), is evident in meaning. And His statement, "al-Warith (the Inheritor)" among the attributes of God, means that He is the One who remains after the destruction of all creation, and it is said that its meaning is that the return of all creatures is to Him.

The Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 15, verse 24:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly know those who go before [you] among you, and We certainly know those who remain behind.﴾ Al-Sha'bi said: its meaning is, "And We certainly know the first of you and the last [of you]." It is also said its meaning is: We know those among you who advance in obedience, and those among you who lag behind in disobedience. It was also said: We know whoever We have created among you, and whoever We will create after them.

It is related from al-Rabi' ibn Anas that the Prophet (ﷺ) urged the people to join in congregational prayer, so some of them advanced and some of them lagged behind because of the crowding of the congregation; so Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And We certainly know those who go before [you] among you, and We certainly know those who remain behind.﴾

It is also said its meaning is: "And We certainly know those among you who advance in regard to fighting, and We know those who hold back from it." In the verse there is a connected report (khabar musnad) transmitted through Abu al-Jawza' from Ibn 'Abbas: that a woman used to attend the congregational prayer, and she was among the most beautiful of women in appearance, so some people would advance forward so as not to see her, and some would hang back. When they bowed, they would look at her from beneath their armpits; so Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse. Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi cited it in his Jami'.

Almost done. Translating the passage:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, your Lord—it is He who will gather them﴾ means: He will gather them unto the Resurrection. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is All-Wise, All-Knowing﴾ means: All-Wise in His management, All-Knowing of His creation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 26:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And We created man from clay of molded sound (ṣalṣāl) from black mud altered (ḥama' masnūn)﴾. Al-ṣalṣāl is the dry clay which, when it is moved, makes a sound (ṣalṣala), i.e., a noise. The poet said:

(And a plain in which you see ṣalṣāl, and below it a plain of hillocks, with its shoulders and joints)

It is also said: al-ṣalṣāl means foul-smelling. It is said: "ṣalla al-laḥm" when the meat became putrid. Al-Kalbi related from Ibn ʿAbbas that al-ṣalṣāl is moist clay. It is also said: when water flows over the earth, making it muddy, and then the water recedes and the earth cracks until it appears like pottery (khazaf), then it is ṣalṣāl.

As for His words: ﴿from black mud altered﴾, al-ḥama' is al-ḥama'a, which is black mud. Al-masnūn is that which has changed and become foul-smelling; so Mujahid said. Some said: al-masnūn is that which is poured out, and this resembles the view we explained, that ṣalṣāl is moist clay. In the reports it is related that al-Hasan used to pour water over his face in a flowing manner (sann), i.e., pour it.

In the verse there is a third view: that al-masnūn is that which is poured into a mold and form. In some (tafsirs) it is mentioned that God Almighty kneaded the clay of Adam and left it until it became altered, black and foul-smelling, and then created Adam from it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 27:

His saying: ﴿And the jinn We created before from the fire of scorching wind.﴾ It is said: al-Jann (the jinn) is Iblis, and it is said: al-Jann is the father of the jinn, just as Adam is the father of mankind. As for Iblis, he is the father of the devils (shayatin). Among the jinn there are believers and disbelievers, and they live and die.

As for the shayatin, there is no Muslim among them, and they die when Iblis dies. Wahb ibn Munabbih mentioned that among the jinn there are those who beget offspring, and they eat and drink in the manner of the children of Adam, and among the jinn there are those who are like the wind: they do not beget, do not eat, and do not drink. And Allah knows best.

As for His saying ﴿from the fire of scorching wind﴾, it means: from hot wind. As-samum (the scorching wind) is a hot wind that enters the pores of a person and kills him. It is said: as-samum is by day and al-harur is by night. It is also said: as-samum is both by night and by day together. And it was said: "nar as-samum" means the blazing flame of fire.

In some reports from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: this samum that we see is a part of seventy parts of the samum of Hell. And it is said: "from the fire of as-samum" means: from the fire of Hell.
God Most High said: ﴿And when your Lord said to the angels, "I am creating a human from clay, from black mud altered and molded"﴾. We have already discussed it.

**The words of the Exalted: ﴿When I have fashioned him﴾, i.e., shaped him. And His words: ﴿and breathed into him of My spirit﴾. The ruh (spirit) is a subtle body by which a human being lives. [He] attributed it to Himself as an honour and a dignity.**

**And His words: ﴿so fall down before him in prostration﴾, i.e., cast yourselves down before him, prostrating.**

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 30:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So the angels prostrated, all of them together﴾. In some tafsirs it is said that He (Allah) said to a group of the angels: "Prostrate to Adam," but they did not do so; so a fire came and burned them all. Then He said to another group: "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except Iblis.

As for His words ﴿all of them together﴾, there is a well-known question concerning it, namely: it is said, since He has said ﴿so the angels prostrated﴾, what is the benefit of His words ﴿all of them together﴾?

The answer: al-Khalil (al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Farahidi, the grammarian) and Sibawayh (the grammarian) both held that this is emphasis after emphasis (ta'kid ba'd ta'kid). Al-Mubarrad (the grammarian) mentioned that His words ﴿so the angels prostrated﴾ could allow for the possibility that some of them had prostrated, so He mentioned ﴿all of them﴾ to remove this ambiguity. Then it was possible that they prostrated at different times, so He mentioned ﴿together (ajma'un)﴾ to remove the confusion.
And His saying: ﴿Except Iblis, who refused to be among those who prostrated﴾ — its meaning is apparent.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He said, "O Iblis, what is [the matter] with you that you are not among those who prostrate?"﴾ Its meaning: Why did you not prostrate when I had commanded you?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 33:

His saying: ﴿He said: "I will not prostrate myself to a human whom You have created from clay, from black mud altered in form."﴾ Its meaning: "I am better than him, because he is of clay, and I am of fire, and fire consumes clay."

In some reports: "Allah the Exalted created the angels from the light of glory, created the jinn from fire, and created Adam from dust."

If it is said: If, according to you, Iblis is one of the angels, and they were created from light, then how did Iblis say, "You created me from fire"?

The answer to this: Iblis was from a class (qabilah) of the angels who were created from fire, and we have mentioned this in Surah al-Baqarah.

"His saying: ﴿Said: "Then get out of it, for you are accursed. And indeed, upon you is the curse until the Day of Recompense."﴾ Its meaning is apparent. And it is said: Iblis is cursed by the heavens and the earth, and the people of the heavens curse him just as the people of the earth curse him."

"His saying: ﴿Said: "Then get out of it, for you are accursed. And indeed, upon you is the curse until the Day of Recompense."﴾ Its meaning is apparent. And it is said: Iblis is cursed by the heavens and the earth, and the people of the heavens curse him just as the people of the earth curse him."

Almighty Allah's saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord, reprieve me until the day they are resurrected."﴾ That is: grant me respite until the Day of Resurrection. The accursed one intended that he would not die; so Allah Most High answered him and said:

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verses 37–38:

﴿Indeed, you are among those given respite﴾ until ﴿the day of the time appointed﴾. That is, the time when all creatures die. It is said that the duration of Iblis's death is forty years, and that is the interval between the two blasts (al-nafkhatayn, the two blasts of the Trumpet). The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: when Iblis asked to be granted respite, God's granting it to him was not an honour for him; rather, it was an increase in his wretchedness and his affliction.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verses 37–38:

﴿Indeed, you are among those given respite﴾ until ﴿the day of the time appointed﴾. That is, the time when all creatures die. It is said that the duration of Iblis's death is forty years, and that is the interval between the two blasts (al-nafkhatayn, the two blasts of the Trumpet). The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: when Iblis asked to be granted respite, God's granting it to him was not an honour for him; rather, it was an increase in his wretchedness and his affliction.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 39:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Lord, because You have led me astray﴾. Most of the scholars hold that its meaning is: "because You have misguided me" (bima adlaltani). It has been said: "because You have deprived me of Your mercy" (bima khaybatani min rahmatika). It has been said: "because You have destroyed me" (bima ahlaktani). It is also said: "because You have attributed to me misguidance" (bima nasabtani ila al-ghiwaya). This last is an interpretation that is false according to the People of the Sunnah.

As for His saying: ﴿I will surely make the earth seem fair to them﴾, its meaning is: I will surely make the love of this world and misguidance seem fair to them. And His saying: ﴿and I will surely mislead them all﴾, that is: I will surely misguide them all. What is meant by Iblis's misleading (ighwa') is his causing them to go astray (tasabbubuhu ila al-ghiwaya).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 40:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Except Your sincere servants among them﴾. "Al-mukhlisin" (the sincere ones, those made pure for God): its meaning is apparent, and we have explained it before.

The Qur'an, Surah 15, verse 41:

The words of the Most High: ﴿This is a straight path to Me﴾. Most of the scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) hold that the verse is a threat and a warning, like a man saying to another, "Your path is upon me, your going is to me," meaning, "You will not escape from me." This is the sense of the Most High's words: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful﴾, that is, over the path of the creatures.

The second opinion regarding the verse: the meaning of His words ﴿This is upon Me﴾ is "to Me."

And His words ﴿straight﴾ mean "by My command and My will."

The third opinion: "This is a path upon Me, straight," meaning: upon Me is its straightness, through clarification, proof, success, and guidance. Al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin recited, "This is a lofty path (sirat ali) straight," meaning lofty. They expressed it as: lofty, so that it cannot be reached, straight, so that it cannot be turned aside. The poet said, using sirat in the sense of "path":

(The Commander of the Faithful is upon a path... when the watering places become crooked, it is straight.)

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them, except those who follow you among the deviators.﴾ This is a confirmation of His saying, mentioned earlier: ﴿except Your sincere servants among them.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 43:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed, Hell is the promised place for them all﴾. He means: the promised place of Iblis and of those who follow him, for abiding therein forever.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 44:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It has seven gates﴾. It is narrated from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Seven gates, some above others." Ibn Jurayj said: The Fire has seven levels (darakat): the first of them is Jahannam, then Laza, then al-Hutamah, then al-Saʿir, then Saqar, then al-Jahim, then al-Hawiyah.

And His saying: ﴿For each gate there is a portion allotted﴾, meaning: for each level there is a people who dwell in it according to the measure of their sins. In some reports it is said: in the first level are the [Muslims], meaning those who were admitted to the Fire according to the measure of their sins and then come out of it; in the second are the Christians, in the third the Jews, in the fourth the [Sabians], in the fifth the Magians, in the sixth the people of polytheism, and in the seventh the [hypocrites].

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 45:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be in gardens and springs﴾. That is: in orchards and rivers.

Their saying: ﴿Enter it in peace, secure.﴾ That is: it is said to them, "Enter it in peace, secure." As for "peace" (al-salam), it means safety, and "security" (al-amn) means being safe from death and from being expelled.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 47:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts﴾. Regarding this, in reports traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "The believers will be detained at a bridge (qantara) between the Fire and the Garden, and retribution will be exacted among them for one another, until, when they have been purified and cleansed, and the resentment has been removed from their hearts, they will be ordered into the Garden."

As for the ghill (resentment), it has been said that it is enmity and hostility; and it has been said that it is spite, envy and treachery. The poet said:

(May God repay us for Jamra, the daughter of Nawfal, a repayment for a treacherous (maghill) liar in trust.)

That is: a traitor (khā'in).

In some reports: the people of the Garden will reach the gate of the Garden while resentment is in their breasts, and when they enter, all resentment will be removed from their breasts.

It is well known from ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him) that he said: "I hope that I, Talha and al-Zubayr will be among those of whom God the Exalted said: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts, as brothers, upon couches facing one another﴾."

As for His words: ﴿upon couches facing one another﴾, that means that none of them will look at the back of another. In some reports from the Prophet: "When a believer in the Garden wishes to meet his believing brother, the couch of each of them will travel toward the other, and they will meet and converse, then each of them will return to his own abode."

**God's words: ﴿They will not be touched therein by fatigue﴾.** That is: exhaustion. **His words: ﴿Nor will they ever be removed from it﴾.** This is the most explicit verse in the Qur'an on *khulud* (eternal abiding), so said the scholars.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verses 49–50:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾. It is related that the Prophet (ﷺ) went out to the Companions while they were laughing, and he said to them: "Do you laugh while the Fire is before you?" Then Jibril came with this verse and said: "Your Lord says to you: O Muhammad, why do you make My servants despair?"

As for His saying: ﴿That I am the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾, its meaning is apparent.

Abu Hurayrah related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "If the believer knew what Allah has of mercy, none would despair of His Paradise; and if the disbeliever knew what Allah has of punishment, none would hope for His Paradise." And Muslim included in his Sahih something close to this.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verses 49–50:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾. It is related that the Prophet (ﷺ) went out to the Companions while they were laughing, and he said to them: "Do you laugh while the Fire is before you?" Then Jibril came with this verse and said: "Your Lord says to you: O Muhammad, why do you make My servants despair?"

As for His saying: ﴿That I am the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾, its meaning is apparent.

"His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And inform them about the guests of Abraham﴾. It was said: its meaning is 'about the guests of Abraham' (in the plural), and we have already explained the number of the angels who were his guests."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 52:

And His saying: ﴿When they entered upon him and said, "Peace!"﴾ means: they greeted him with a greeting of peace (salaman).

And His saying: ﴿He said, "Indeed, we are fearful of you."﴾ The reason for Ibrahim's fear of them was that he brought the food near to them and they did not eat it, and when a guest did not eat, they would become suspicious of him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 15, verse 53:

﴿They said, "Do not be afraid."﴾ That is: do not fear (la takhaf). The poet said:

(By your life, I do not know, and indeed I am apprehensive ... over which of us death will reach first.)

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, We give you good tidings of a boy who will be learned﴾ means: a boy in his youth, learned in his adulthood, and he is Isaac.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿He said: "Do you give me good tidings?"﴾ The original form is أبشرتمونني (abshartumūnanī), so one of the two nūns was dropped and the kasra was retained (as an indicator of the first person).

His saying: ﴿Although old age has reached me?﴾ means: "in the state of old age." This is said in the manner of wonder (ta'ajjub, expressing amazement), and likewise His saying: ﴿Then by what will you give good tidings?﴾ is in the manner of wonder, not in the manner of doubt (shakk) or denial (inkar).

"His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They said, "We give you good news of the truth, so do not be of those who despair."﴾ Al-haqq (the truth): placing a thing in its proper place as wisdom calls for. Al-qunut is despair (al-ya's), and the meaning of al-haqq here is truthfulness (al-sidq)."

Almost all of the passage is a Qur'anic quotation or a plain explanatory statement, so I translate it directly.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except the misguided?"﴾ He means: except the disbelievers. And despair of the mercy of God is one of the major sins, like feeling safe from the plotting of God.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He said, "Then what is your business, O messengers?"﴾ We have already explained its meaning in Surah Hud.
Allah's words: ﴿They said, "Indeed, we have been sent to a criminal people."﴾ He meant by this the people of Lut.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verses 59–60:

And His saying: ﴿except the family of Lot﴾: what is meant by it is Lot, his daughters, and those who believed in him, and we have already mentioned this. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, We will save them all together﴾: this is an exception from an exception. The first exception is from those who are destroyed, and the second is from those who are saved. So what remains of the excepted party by the second exception is among those destroyed, and that is his wife. This is like when a man says to you: "I owe you ten, except four, except three." The party excepted by the second exception remains within what he acknowledged by the first acknowledgment, so it becomes as if he had excepted one dirham, and nine dirhams become due.

And His saying: ﴿We have decreed﴾, meaning: We have judged. And His saying: ﴿that she is among those who remain behind﴾, meaning: among those who remain in the punishment. The poet said:

(Do not strike the she-camels on their rear ends... for you do not know who is the one that gives birth.)

Meaning: with their remnants. And in the hadiths: "The people of knowledge will depart and remnants (ghabarat) will remain in vessels of evil," meaning: remnants.

And His saying: ﴿except the family of Lot﴾: what is meant by it is Lot, his daughters, and those who believed in him, and we have already mentioned this. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, We will save them all together﴾: this is an exception from an exception. The first exception is from those who are destroyed, and the second is from those who are saved. (Do not strike the she-camels on their rear ends... for you do not know who is the one that gives birth.)

Meaning: with their remnants. And in the hadiths: "The people of knowledge will depart and remnants (ghabarat) will remain in vessels of evil," meaning: remnants.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So when the messengers came to the family of Lot﴾. Its meaning is apparent.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He said, "Indeed, you are a people unknown."﴾ Because he did not recognize them.

"They said, 'Rather, we have brought you that about which they used to doubt.'" Meaning: they used to dispute (or be in doubt). In the account, Lot used to threaten them with the punishment, but they would not believe him, so this is the sense of His words: ﴿that about which they used to doubt﴾.
And His saying: ﴿And We have brought you the truth, and indeed We are truthful﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 65:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So travel with your family﴾ — "sara" (سرى) and "asra" (أسرى) have the same meaning. His saying: ﴿in a portion of the night﴾ means: in a part of the night. His saying: ﴿and follow their backs﴾ is evidence that God, the Exalted, commanded him to send his family ahead, then to proceed following in their tracks.

His saying: ﴿and let none of you look back﴾ — He commanded them to refrain from looking back, so that they would not be terrified by the punishment when it descended upon their people. It was also said: God, the Exalted, made that a sign for whoever of the family of Lot would be saved, for the woman looked back when she heard the crash, and so she perished.

His saying: ﴿and go where you are commanded﴾ — it is said: they were commanded to proceed to "Zughar" (زغر), which is a town in al-Sham (Greater Syria). It was also said: to the land of al-Urdunn (Jordan) and Filastin (Palestine).

"The Exalted's statement: ﴿And We decreed that matter to him﴾. We have already mentioned that al-qada' (decree; the root sense of completion, finishing) means al-faragh (completion), and its meaning is: We judged and finalized the matter which We had commanded concerning the people of Lut. And His statement: ﴿that the last remnant of these will be cut off at dawn﴾ — i.e., the root (dabir) of these people; it is also said: the last (akhir) of these. ﴿Cut off, entering upon the morning﴾ — meaning: at the time they enter into the morning (al-subh)."
The Exalted said: ﴿And the people of the city came, rejoicing.﴾ That is, they gave one another good news, because of what they hoped for: committing the abomination (al-fahisha).

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "Indeed, these are my guests, so do not disgrace me."﴾ Al-fadiha (disgrace): an action done to a person that brings upon him shame (al-ar), and [the feeling of] indignation (al-anfa).
﴿So fear Allah and do not disgrace me.﴾ Al-khizy means disgrace (al-fadiha).

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They said, "Did we not forbid you from [harboring] the worlds?"﴾ Its meaning: "Did we not forbid you from hosting anyone?" It was also said: "Did we not forbid you from the worlds," meaning: bringing strangers into the town, for if you bring them in, we will commit indecency with them.
﴿He said, "These are my daughters, if you must act."﴾ We have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 72:

And His saying: ﴿By your life, indeed they are in their intoxication, wandering blindly.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "By your life (wa 'aishika)." It was also said: "By your life (wa hayatika)." It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "Allah did not create any creature more noble before Him than Muhammad (ﷺ), for Allah the Exalted did not swear by the life of anyone except the life of Muhammad (ﷺ)." And His saying: ﴿in their intoxication, wandering blindly⁠﴾, meaning: in their misguidance they wander back and forth (yata'addadun).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 73:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So the Cry seized them at sunrise﴾. It is said: "ashraqat al-shams" (the sun rose/shone) when it has risen. If it is asked: He said before this, ﴿at early morning﴾, and here He said, ﴿at sunrise﴾; so how is the reconciliation (wajh al-jam') to be understood?

The answer is in two respects. The first: the beginning of the punishment was at dawn (al-subh), and its completion was at sunrise (al-ishraq).

The second answer: "ishraq" here means "isbah" (entering the morning), and this is permissible in the speech of the Arabs.

And His saying: ﴿So We made its highest part its lowest﴾ has already been explained.

And His saying: ﴿and We rained upon them stones of baked clay﴾ has already been explained.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 75:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for those who observe with insight﴾. That is: for those who look and take heed (al-mu'tabirin).

It has also been said: for those who are perceptive (al-mutafarrisin), namely those who know people by their appearance (bi-simahum) according to what Allah shows them of it.

It has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Beware of the insight (firasa) of the believer, for he looks with the light of Allah." It was related by ʿAṭiyya, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi mentioned it in his Jami'.

And Thabit narrated from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Among my community there are people who know others by their tawassum (signs of character)."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 76:

And His saying: ﴿And indeed it is on a road that remains﴾, meaning: on a clear road that is not hidden and does not vanish. He called it "remaining" because of the signs that persist upon it, and they used to pass by it on their journeys to Syria and on their return.
And His saying: ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign for the believers﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verses 78–79:

Regarding His statement, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, the companions of the Thicket were wrongdoers.﴾ The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: "in" (inna) is for emphasis (ta'kid), and likewise the lam in His statement ﴿wrongdoers﴾ is for emphasis. The meaning of the verse is: "The companions of the Thicket were indeed wrongdoers."

Al-Ayka (the Thicket) is al-ghaydah (a dense thicket of trees). It is also said that it is the intertwined trees. Qatadah said: "Their trees were doum palms." Some of them said: "Their trees bore fruit, and they ate from them fresh in summer and dry in winter." He said in another place: ﴿Laykah⦆ (the Companions of Laykah). Regarding this there are two opinions. The first: al-Ayka and Laykah have the same meaning. The second: al-Ayka is the name of the region, and Laykah is the name of the town.

The people of exegesis said: "Their messenger was the Prophet Shu'ayb, and he was sent to the people of Madyan and to the people of al-Ayka. As for the people of Madyan, they were destroyed by the Cry (al-sayhah). As for the people of al-Ayka, they were destroyed by the torment of the [Cloud] (al-zullah)."

In the narrative: a severe heat afflicted them in their dwellings, and God the Exalted withheld the wind from them and intensified the heat upon them. They remained in this state for days. Then the valley blazed with fire over them, and they were all destroyed. It is said: they perished from distress (ghamm). This is the meaning of His statement: ﴿So We took vengeance upon them﴾.

As for His statement: ﴿And indeed, both of them are on a clear road (imam mubin).﴾ That is, on an evident path. The path was called an imam because it is followed and taken as a model (yu'tamm bihi wa tuba'). The pronoun in His statement ﴿both of them﴾ refers to the town of the people of Lot and the town of the companions of the Thicket. These lands lie between the Hijaz and al-Sham, and the Quraysh used to pass by them on their journeys.

Corrected rendering, as requested:

And His saying: ﴿So the Cry seized them at dawn﴾. That is: when they had entered into the morning.
And His saying: ﴿So what they had been earning did not avail them﴾ — i.e., what they had been earning did not ward off from them (the punishment).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 85:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth﴾, meaning: to make the truth manifest. The connection of this with what precedes it in meaning is that when they denied the truth, We destroyed them, because We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth. It is also said: the meaning of "truth" is the recompense of the one who does good for his good, and the recompense of the one who does evil for his evil.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed the Hour is coming﴾, meaning: so that recompense for good and evil will become manifest.

And His saying: ﴿So forgive with gracious forgiveness﴾, meaning: turn away from them without impatience or complaint.

Ibn 'Abbas said: this was before the revelation of the verse of the sword, and then it was abrogated by the verse of the sword.
And His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is the Creator, the All-Knowing﴾ means: the Creator, the All-Knowing of His creation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 87:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated and the great Qur'an.﴾ There is difference of opinion regarding this. It is narrated from ʿUmar, ʿAli, and ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud (in one of the two narrations), as well as Mujahid and Qatadah, that they said: it is al-Fatihah (the Opening chapter of the Book). This has also been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) through the narration of Adam ibn Abi Iyas, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Saʿid al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Al-hamdu lillah (Praise be to Allah): it is the Mother of the Book, the seven oft-repeated, and the great Qur'an."

The Shaykh, the Imam, the most honoured, Shaykh al-Islam Abu al-Muzaffar said: al-Makki ibn ʿAbd al-Razzaq al-Kushmayhani informed us, saying: my grandfather Abu al-Haytham Muhammad ibn al-Makki informed us, saying: al-Firabri informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari informed us, from Adam ibn Abi Iyas... [the report to its end].

They differed concerning Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. ʿAli and Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is the seventh verse. Abu Hurayrah, Mujahid and Qatadah said: it is not a verse of it, and the seventh verse is His saying: ﴿The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour.﴾

Ubayy ibn Kaʿb narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There was sent down to me a surah the like of which was not sent down in the Torah or the Gospel: it is Umm al-Qur'an, the seven oft-repeated, and the great Qur'an which I have been given." Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi mentioned it in his Jami'.

The second opinion regarding the verse: that the seven oft-repeated are the seven long ones (al-Tiwal), the singular of tiwal being tuwla, and they are: al-Baqarah, Al ʿImran, al-Nisa', al-Ma'idah, al-An'am, al-A'raf, and Yunus. This is what is transmitted, and it is the saying of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAbbas, in the narration of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, and it is the saying of al-Hasan al-Basri and a group of the Successors (tabiʿun).

A third opinion regarding the verse: that the seven oft-repeated are: commands, prohibitions, good tidings, warnings, the coining of parables, the enumeration of blessings, and the reports of earlier generations.

As for the meaning of "al-mathani" (the oft-repeated): if we take the verse to refer to al-Fatihah, then its meaning is that it is repeated in every rak'ah. It was also said: because in it is the praise (thana') of Allah, the Exalted. Here "min" (from) is for specification of kind (li-al-tajnis), not for partitive meaning (li-al-tab'id), like His saying: ﴿So avoid the filth of idols﴾. Some of them mentioned that the meaning of the verse is: "And We have certainly given you seven [parts] of the Qur'an which is oft-repeated," and the Qur'an was called oft-repeated because its rulings, stories, parables and lessons are repeated within it; so on this reading "min" is partitive. As for the view we stated, that the seven oft-repeated are the seven long ones, they were named oft-repeated because reports, parables, lessons and stories are repeated in them.

As for His saying: ﴿and the great Qur'an﴾, what is meant by it is the rest of the Qur'an apart from al-Fatihah. In this there is great honour for al-Fatihah, since He singled it out for mention and for the favour bestowed upon him through it, then mentioned the rest of the Qur'an. According to the second opinion, the great Qur'an is the seven long ones and others, and He singled out the seven long ones for mention to honour them. The poet said:

(I adjure you by the dwelling of the Criterion... the Mother of the Book, the seven of the oft-repeated)

((Two)) of the verses of the Qur'an...

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 88:

The words of God, Exalted: ﴿Do not extend your eyes toward what We have given enjoyment to pairs of them, nor grieve over them⁠—﴾ The connection of this with what precedes it is that when He bestowed upon him the Qur'an, He forbade him from desiring the world and from looking at its adornment and competing with its people for it. Abu 'Ubayd narrated that Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna said regarding the meaning of his saying (ﷺ): "He is not of us who does not chant the Qur'an (yataghanna bil-Qur'an)," that is: he does not seek sufficiency (yastaghni) through the Qur'an. Then he interpreted this verse accordingly: ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated [verses] and the great Qur'an. Do not extend your eyes toward what We have given enjoyment to pairs of them⁠—﴾ on this basis.

In a report from the Prophet (ﷺ) he said: "Whoever is given the Qur'an and then thinks that someone else has been given something better than what he has been given has belittled something great and magnified something small."

As for His saying: ﴿pairs of them﴾, its meaning is: kinds of them, namely the Jews, the Christians and the rest of the polytheists. It was also said: they are the wealthy.

As for His saying: ﴿nor grieve over them⁠—﴾ it means: do not be distressed over what has escaped you of sharing with them in the world. In some of the exegetical works, from Abu Rafi': "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had a guest come to him, and he had nothing to offer him. So he sent to a Jew to borrow food from him until the new moon of Rajab. The Jew said: 'By God, I will not give it to you except against a pledge.' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'I am trustworthy to God in the heavens and on the earth. Had he sold to me or lent to me, I would have repaid him.' Then he pawned his coat of mail with him. So God, Exalted, revealed: ﴿Do not extend your eyes toward what We have given enjoyment to⁠—﴾."

As for His saying: ﴿And lower your wing to the believers⁠—﴾ it means: soften your side toward the believers.
And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And say, "Indeed, I am the clear warner."﴾ [i.e., clear in conveying the truth].

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 90:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿As We sent down upon the dividers﴾. If someone says: what is the meaning of the kaf (ka, "as") here, given that it indicates comparison? The answer to this is that its meaning is: "I warn you of a punishment that will descend upon you, just as We sent down punishment upon the dividers (al-muqtasimin)." It is also said that the kaf is a connecting particle (silah), and its meaning is: "Say: I am the clear warner of what We sent down upon the dividers."

As for the meaning of "the dividers" (al-muqtasimin), there are several opinions. The first: they are the Jews and the Christians, and the meaning of "dividing" (al-iqtisam) regarding them is that they believed in some of the Books and disbelieved in others. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas.

The second view: they are the Quraysh, and the meaning of "dividing" is that they divided their speech about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Some of them said: "He is a soothsayer (kahin)," some of them said: "He is a sorcerer (sahir)," and some of them said: "He is a poet (shair)."

The third view: al-Farra' mentioned that the people of Makkah sent groups onto the roads of those arriving at Makkah during the season of pilgrimage (al-mawsim), so that they would say to whoever they met of those arriving at Makkah: "Do not approach Muhammad." They would ask them about his condition, and some of them would say: "He is a soothsayer," some would say: "He is a madman," some would say: "He is a sorcerer," and some would say: "He is a poet." The meaning of "dividing" is that they divided the roads of Makkah among themselves. This is a well-known view, reported by Mujahid, Qatadah and others.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 91:

And His saying: ﴿Those who have made the Qur'an into parts﴾. Abu 'Ubayda said: "'Idin (ʿiḍīn) is derived from al-i'diya' (the dividing into parts)." Al-Farra' claimed that it is derived from al-'idah (the parts, or the rock-fragments), and al-Kisa'i said: "It is permissible that it be derived from both of them." The meaning of the verse is that they made the Qur'an into fragments and pieces: some of them said, "It is the fables of the ancients," and some of them said, "It is soothsaying," and what is similar to this.

There is another opinion regarding the verse: namely, that the meaning of His saying ﴿'idin﴾ (ʿiḍīn) is: they named it sorcery. The ʿidha (ʿiḍa) is sorcery, so ʿidha and ʿidīn have one meaning, like ʿizza and ʿizīn. The poet said:

(And the religion of God is not to be divided ...)

Meaning: scattered.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verses 92–93:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely call them all to account for what they used to do﴾. It is narrated from Anas, on the authority of the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "It is the statement: there is no god but Allah." And it is narrated from Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi that he said: "All creation will be questioned about two things: about monotheism (tawhid), and about their response to the messengers." It has also been said: the meaning of His words ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely call them all to account for what they used to do﴾ is: all the deeds they perform that fall within the scope of legal obligation (taklif).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verses 92–93:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely call them all to account for what they used to do﴾. It is narrated from Anas, on the authority of the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "It is the statement: there is no god but Allah." And it is narrated from Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi that he said: "All creation will be questioned about two things: about monotheism (tawhid), and about their response to the messengers." It has also been said: the meaning of His words ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely call them all to account for what they used to do﴾ is: all the deeds they perform that fall within the scope of legal obligation (taklif).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 94:

The words of Allah the Exalted: [﴿So proclaim openly what you are commanded﴾]. Al-Qutaybi said: its meaning is: make it manifest (ižhar) what you are commanded, and do not be concerned with anyone's watching. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been concealing himself until Allah the Exalted revealed this verse and commanded him to make it public. Some of them said: the meaning of His words ﴿So proclaim openly what you are commanded﴾ is: separate, by means of the Qur'an, truth from falsehood. Mujahid mentioned that the meaning of His words ﴿fasda'﴾ is: declare openly with the Qur'an, and he (the Prophet) had been reciting in a low voice (musirran) out of fear of the polytheists; so Allah the Exalted commanded him to recite aloud and not to care about them.

In the language, al-sada' (the splitting, breaking open) is derived from manifestness, and from it comes al-sadi' (ṣadīʿ), a name for the dawn, the poet said:

(As if they were a rabab, and as if he were / a gambler's arrow-dealer pouring out and splitting (the lots))

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And turn away from the polytheists﴾, meaning: turn away from their replies, for none answers a fool with foolishness except a fool.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 95:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We suffice you against the mockers﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: The mockers (al-mustahzi'un) were five men: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, and ʿAdi ibn Qays. Some have added to these al-Harith ibn al-Tulatila and al-Harith ibn Ghaytala. What is related from Ibn ʿAbbas is what we have explained. It is narrated: "Jibril was standing with the Prophet (ﷺ), and these people passed by them one by one. Jibril would say to the Prophet: What is your opinion of this man? The Prophet would say: Evil is this servant of Allah. Then Jibril would say: We have sufficed you against him. So they perished. As for al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, he passed by an arrow, which caught on his garment; he went to sit down and it cut his main artery (akhhal), and he bled out and died. As for al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, he passed over a thorn, which scratched his leg, and his flesh fell away from it, and he died. As for al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth, he was struck on his face with a branch of thorn, and his eyeballs ran out, and he died, and he kept saying: I was answered in the supplication of Muhammad. As for ʿAdi ibn Qays and al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, one of them stood up at night and a snake stung him, and he died; as for the other, he was afflicted with thirst, and he kept drinking until his belly burst and he perished." This is the meaning of ﴿the sufficing against the mockers﴾.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who set up another god alongside God, but they will come to know﴾. He described them as associating others with God (shirk) and worshipping idols. His saying, ﴿but they will come to know﴾, is a threat and a warning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 97:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And We know that your breast is constricted by what they say﴾. This is a consolation [for the Prophet]. It has been related in some tafsir works that when Allah the Exalted sent down in the Qur'an the surah of al-'Ankabut (The Spider), the surah of al-Naml (The Ant), the surah of al-Dhubab (The Fly), and the surah of al-Nahl (The Bee), they would gather and say in mockery: "This one points to the surah of the Ant, and this one points to the surah of the Fly, and this one points to the surah of the Spider, and this one points to the surah of the Bee," and what is similar to that. So Allah the Exalted sent down ﴿And We know that your breast is constricted by what they say﴾. This is the mockery mentioned in the preceding verse.

And His saying: ﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise﴾. Tasbih (glorification) is praising Allah by declaring Him free of imperfections and exalted above defects. It was also said: pray, by the command of your Lord. In a report from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her: "The Prophet (ﷺ), whenever a matter distressed him, would resort to prayer." And His saying: ﴿And be among those who prostrate﴾, meaning: among those who pray.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 15, verse 99:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾. That is: death.

If someone says: Would the words ﴿And worship your Lord﴾ not have sufficed? What is the benefit of His words ﴿until there comes to you the certainty﴾?

We say: Had He limited Himself to His words ﴿And worship your Lord﴾, then whoever worshipped once would have fulfilled the requirement of the command. So He said ﴿until there comes to you the certainty﴾, so that one persists in it until he dies. This verse is similar in meaning to the verse he mentioned afterwards, which is in Maryam, namely the words of the Exalted: ﴿And He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive﴾.

In the reports traced back (musnad) through the narration of Jubayr ibn Nufayr from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Allah did not command me to gather wealth or to be among the merchants, but He commanded me to pray and to be among those who prostrate, and to worship my Lord until the certainty comes to me."
